thread:
Jordan (CSM): Heads up — Polestar onboarding flagged for SLA alignment. Renewal in ~6 weeks, they saw week-over-week latency/uplift and are asking for a remediation + credits breakdown. Target: uptime 99.9% + 95th pctl latency SLO. We need a short customer note and an internal fix plan. @Eli @Marco @Priya
Eli (SRE): Looking at traces — two ~20m latency spikes last Tue tied to cold starts and one EU failover. Also some tails from large batch jobs.
Marco (Solutions Engineer): Do we have a precedent for onboarding credits? Want to be consistent but also keep renewal healthy.
Jordan (CSM): They prefer a transparent, math-first reply (no long legal prose). Quick chart + proposed credit works.
SRE Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-328 (linked logs + perf dump).
Eli (SRE): Proposed quick mitigations: 1) enable prefix/KV warm cache for Polestar routes 2) set min-instances=2 in EU at night window 3) tune batching threshold from 16->8 for low-latency routes. Expected immediate improvement on cold starts.
Marco (Solutions Engineer): Can we quantify cost impact? Polestar is mid-tier but renewal depends on perceived stability.
Eli (SRE): Rough estimate: extra reserved capacity ~ +$750/month. I'll give exact numbers in a short runbook.
Priya (Account Manager): I'll draft customer note — they want either a one-off credit or service ramp assurances. Which do we recommend?
Jordan (CSM): Offer: prorated credit for the degraded week + a free enablement session and a short-term capacity bump while they finish warmup. Keep it simple.
Eli (SRE): Credit calc (example): 
`credit = invoice * max(0, (SLO - actual_uptime) / SLO)`
Example: SLO 99.9% vs actual 99.65% over billing period -> delta 0.25% -> credit = 0.0025 * invoice (small). I'll attach numbers.
Marco (Solutions Engineer): That formula looks fine for quick comms. For bigger gaps we use tiered credits per contract, but this is onboarding noise.
Jordan (CSM): Priya can you confirm whether they want the numeric credit or prefer a service credit statement? Small numeric credit is often easier.
Priya (Account Manager): I'll ask them in the note. Also asking for acceptance window.
Eli (SRE): I'll produce: - short runbook + rollback steps - per-route latency export (CSV) - heatmap for last 30 days.
Jordan (CSM): Goal: send customer-facing note by EOD Friday. Who owns what?
Priya (Account Manager): I'll own the note and the ask. Jordan, can you review?
Jordan (CSM): Yep. Eli — attach runbook + cost delta by tomorrow noon.
Eli (SRE): Will do. Also suggest long-term target bump to 99.95% for this account once warm caching is in place.
Marco (Solutions Engineer): I'll schedule a 30-min enablement session next week with Polestar infra; propose demo of prefix caching and warmup best practices.
Jordan (CSM): Awesome. Quick action items: 
- Priya: draft + send note by EOD Fri
- Eli: runbook, cost delta, CSV/heatmap by Thu noon
- Marco: schedule enablement 30-min slot next week
- Jordan: review note + follow-up comms
Jordan (CSM): Thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya (Account Manager): One more ask — can we include a simple SLA one-pager in the email (bullet list + what triggers credits)? That usually calms customers.
Eli (SRE): I'll attach a 1-page SLA summary.
Jordan (CSM): Perfect. Closing this thread when note is sent.
Priya (Account Manager): On it.
SRE Bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up check-in in 10 days (reminder id REM-2026-44).
